The next generation of iPhones is about to arrive, and it will be different. The entry-level iPhone 18 will not make an appearance this time, as that model has been pushed to a spring launch. The focus this September will be entirely on the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the all-new foldable iPhone.

Of course, the most talked-about topic in the market is the price hike. The iPhone 18 Pro series will inevitably be more expensive, which raises a question—is it wise to buy the iPhone 17 Pro at its current price?

What's New in the iPhone 18 Pro

The iPhone 18 Pro will be a modest upgrade over the iPhone 17 Pro, though I wouldn't call it an 'S year.'

There are a few notable new features: a smaller Dynamic Island, a main camera with an adjustable aperture for finer depth-of-field control, new colour options (including a red one), and Apple's in-house C2 modem—the first time the Pro iPhone gets one, which will also enable 5G connectivity via satellite.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max will be thicker and pack a larger battery, which, combined with the C2 modem, should deliver a significant boost in battery life.

There will also be the usual chip upgrade, with the A20 Pro (the first chip built on a second-generation 2nm process) and the N2 networking chip. The iPhone 18 Pro is expected to stick with the same 12GB of RAM as its predecessor. Apple will also redesign the Camera Control button to reduce accidental triggers.

Apple may well surprise us with other upgrades, but the above is everything we know so far.

The Price Hike Issue

This is the most contentious issue right now. Apple has already raised prices significantly across the iPad and Mac lines, and has signalled that more hikes are on the way. The iPhone 18 Pro series is almost certainly going to cost more.

How much more? That's hard to say. Some estimates put the increase at up to $300, but Apple may opt for a more modest bump and sacrifice some margin. I expect the iPhone 18 Pro to start somewhere between $1,199 and $1,399, and the iPhone 18 Pro Max between $1,299 and $1,499.

For most people, this would be a hard pill to swallow—especially when the new iPhone offers little to justify such a steep price increase.

Should You Buy Now?

Ultimately, the decision is yours. Personally, I think the iPhone 17 Pro delivers a new-phone experience largely comparable to the iPhone 18 Pro, yet costs considerably less. That's hard to argue with.

Apple has yet to raise iPhone pricing, so today you can still pick up an iPhone 17 Pro for $1,099 and an iPhone 17 Pro Max for $1,199. If you're on an older iPhone and thinking of upgrading, buying last year's model—even near the end of its cycle—is still the smartest move.

The memory crunch triggered by AI data centres is expected to persist for years, so Apple pricing is unlikely to come down anytime soon. Plan your purchases wisely.
